 J-Beauty Is Trending & Here’s Everything You Need To Know
 K-Beauty might be all the rage, but there’s another East Asian beauty scene worth getting to know. J-Beauty – or Japanese beauty – has a rich heritage of its own, bringing together longstanding brands, innovative formulas and a more ritual-led approach to everything from skincare and make-up to haircare. Some of its best-known names have been around for more than 150 years, while others are behind the viral products you see all over social media. From established names to exciting new launches and treatments, here’s what’s worth knowing…
 By 
 Jenn George 
 / 
 Save To My Favourites
 Images: 
 @SUQQU_Official; @SHIRO_Japan; @Tatcha
 All products on this page have been selected by our editorial team, however we may make commission on some products.
 @Shiseido
 THE HERITAGE BRAND
 Shiseido
 Founded in 1872, Shiseido began life as Japan’s first Western-style pharmacy, bringing together Eastern philosophies and Western science – an approach that continues to inform its formulas today. More than 150 years on, it’s become one of the world’s most recognised beauty brands, with a strong line-up of best-sellers across skincare and make-up. Among the stand-outs are its Ultimune Power Infusing Serum , known for its skin-strengthening benefits, and its glow-giving foundation , which delivers a fresh, radiant finish.
 Visit SHISEIDO.CO.UK 
 Ultimune Power Infusing Serum, £130 
 Revitalessence Glow Foundation, £53 
 Benefiance Wrinkle Smoothing Eye Cream, £75 
 Colorgel Lip Balm, £34 
 @Curel_Japanese_Skincare
 THE SENSITIVE SKINCARE
 Curél
 While much of Japanese and Korean skincare takes a gentle, barrier-first approach, Curél has a particular focus on those prone to dryness and sensitivity. Launched in Japan in 1999 following extensive research into ceramides – naturally occurring lipids that help maintain the skin barrier and lock in moisture – the brand’s formulas are designed to replenish hydration, support the barrier and soothe dry, sensitive skin. Since arriving in the UK in 2019, Curél has built a loyal following, with its Deep Moisture Spray becoming a desk-side and in-flight staple for many beauty editors.
 Visit CUREL.COM 
 Deep Moisture Spray, £19.50 
 Intensive Moisture Facial Cream, £22.50 
 Makeup Cleansing Oil, £16.50 
 @Tatcha
 THE HERO SKINCARE
 Tatcha
 Rooted in Japanese beauty rituals, ingredients and traditions, Tatcha has built a following well beyond its home market. Its international appeal may in part be down to founder Vicky Tsai, who is half-Japanese and half-American, and her understanding of both Eastern and Western approaches to skincare. The brand is known for its luxurious, sensorial textures, designed to turn everyday routines into more of a ritual. Rice, green tea and algae feature throughout the range, including in the much-loved Rice Polish – an innovative powder-to-foam exfoliating cleanser – and the Dewy Skin Cream , a rich moisturiser so popular that the brand claims a pot is sold every minute.
 Visit TATCHA.CO.UK 
 The Dewy Skin Cream, £69 
 The Rice Polish, £65 
 Luminous Dewy Skin Mist, £48 
 THE NEWEST IMPORT
 TAKAMI
 New to the UK this year but already well established in Japan, TAKAMI is a skincare brand rooted in dermatological expertise and a long-term approach to skin health. Born out of a clinic, its products draw on years of patient-first knowledge, with a focus on ‘Kakushitsu Beauty’ – a philosophy focused on caring for the skin’s outer barrier rather than aggressively stripping it back, while still delivering visible results. Its hero product, the Skin Peel , is gentle enough for even sensitive complexions and is loved for its ability to smooth texture and boost radiance. Since launching, it has sold more than 18 million bottles.
 Follow @TAKAMI 
 Daily Renewing Soft Peel, £35 
 Barrier Essential Milk, £35 
 Micro Gel PGA+HA, £39 
 Golden 5C Brightening Serum, £58 
 @TAKAMI
 THE UNIQUE TREATMENT
 Japanese Head Spa
 This is a far cry from your usual trip to the hairdresser. A Japanese head spa is a multi-step treatment dedicated to the hair, scalp and mind, combining everything from a detailed consultation and scalp analysis to a deep cleanse, massage and water-therapy session. The latter often involves a halo-shaped device that gently circulates water over the head, alongside targeted hair treatments and a neck and shoulder massage. Usually carried out on a fully reclining bed, the experience is as much about switching off as it is caring for your hair. Sessions can last up to two hours, finishing with a blow-dry that leaves you feeling thoroughly relaxed and looking polished.
 Visit HEADSPALONDON.COM 
 The Vault Stock
 @SHIRO_Japan
 THE CULT FRAGRANCES
 SHIRO
 If any fragrance brand captures the spirit of Japan, it’s SHIRO. While the range spans everything from skincare to make-up, it’s the scents that have earned the brand its cult following. The aesthetic is understated, the blends are sophisticated and the finished products are delicate without being forgettable. Each one feels effortless to wear, yet has a distinctive quality that stays with you. It may not be a household name just yet but SHIRO is certainly one to know.
 Visit SHIRO-SHIRO.UK 
 Smoked Leather Eau De Parfum, £131 
 Bon Wood Eau De Parfum, £131 
 Salt & Waves Body Mist, £38 
 @AndHoney_Japan
 THE BEST-SELLING HAIRCARE
 &Honey
 Compared to skincare and make-up, Japanese haircare tends to get less attention but &Honey is helping to change that. As the name suggests, honey is at the heart of the formulas, chosen for its nourishing and moisturising properties, with the range designed to leave hair feeling soft, smooth and hydrated. Expect rich, indulgent textures and playful packaging, alongside some impressive numbers: more than 130 million products have been sold globally, making &Honey one of Japan’s biggest haircare success stories.
 Follow @ANDHONEY_JAPAN 
 Deep Moist Shampoo, £15.99 
 Deep Moist Treatment, £15.99 
 @SUQQU_Official
 THE LUXE MAKE-UP
 SUQQU
 Founded in 2003, SUQQU has a strong skincare offering – including its signature ‘Gankin’ massage, which you can often experience at its in-store counters – but it’s the make-up that has really put the brand on the map. Known for its luxurious formulas and beautifully crafted textures, its finely milled powders are particularly sought after, from eyeshadows to blushers. Many feature stunning gradients of colour inspired by Japan’s changing seasons, making them as beautiful to look at as they are to wear.
 Follow @SUQQU_OFFICIAL 
 Signature Color Eyes Eyeshadow, £50 
 The Foundation, £81 
 Blurring Color Blush, £40 
 @CleDePeauBeaute
 THE BEAUTY ICON
 Clé De Peau
 Clé de Peau doesn’t do understated. With its opulent packaging and luxurious feel, the brand’s products look every bit as premium as their price tags suggest. But there’s plenty of substance behind the glamour too. The name translates as ‘the key to skin’s beauty’, with the brand built around a scientific approach to ‘skin intelligence’. Drawing on more than 40 years of skin cell research, its formulas use carefully developed, high-performance ingredients to deliver impressive results. And while its skincare is a major draw, the make-up deserves attention too – particularly the concealer , a long-time favourite among make-up artists.
 Visit CLEDEPEAUBEAUTE.CO.UK 
 Beauté Concealer, £62 
 Beauté Le Sérum, £295 
 Skin Beauty Enhancer, £84
